item.title: Union boss stuns with major Republican endorsement as election nears
item.description: Teamsters president endorsed Senate Republican Ashley Moody in the Florida Senate race, marking a major break from traditional union Democratic ties.
item.content:encoded:
The leader of one of the nation’s oldest and largest unions stunned political observers by issuing a surprise endorsement for a Senate Republican stalwart over the weekend.

Teamsters General President Sean O’Brien, who famously nearly came to blows with now-Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin during a Senate hearing before ultimately becoming acquaintances, issued a ringing endorsement of Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., signaling a major break from national union sentiment that has tended to favor Democrats.

"Just voted in the State of Florida for the first time, and very proud to have cast a ballot for Sen. Ashley Moody," O’Brien, whose 123-year-old union is about 1.3 million-strong, announced Sunday.

5 TAKEAWAYS FROM FLORIDA SENATE PRIMARY: GOP SEN ASHLEY MOODY WILL FACE DSA'S NIXON

"Sen. Moody has been extremely helpful working with the Teamsters to protect workers’ pensions, defend good-paying jobs, and support well-funded union apprenticeship programs."

"The Teamsters look forward to working with Sen. Moody in her role on the Senate HELP Committee to pass the Faster Labor Contracts Act and get this critical legislation signed into law to protect American workers," he added.

FRUSTRATED BLUE-COLLAR UNION BOSSES RIP SOCIALIST POLITICIANS, WARN OF LABOR EXODUS FROM DEM PARTY

O’Brien, a self-described "lifelong Democrat," previously spoke at the 2024 Republican National Convention, but emphasized at the time that the Democratic Party had snubbed his request to speak at its convention.

"If the far-left want to criticize me and attack me, that’s OK. If the far-right wants to do the same, that’s great. I represent 1.3 million hardworking men and women," O’Brien said at the time.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Teamsters as well as Moody’s campaign for comment.

Moody, a former state attorney general, said in a statement that she was proud to have O’Brien’s endorsement:

"I’ll always fight to protect hardworking Americans, strengthen good-paying jobs, and ensure resources are available to train our next generation. It’s been great to deliver for Florida’s working families," she said.

After O’Brien endorsed Moody, the lawmaker’s Democratic opponent responded by posting a photo she once took with O’Brien and writing that "Ashley Moody never walked the line with you."

AOC BACKS FLORIDA DEM ANGIE NIXON FOR US SENATE: 'I’M PROUD TO ENDORSE HER'

"But ok brother. Shout out to all the rank and file Teamsters that are voting for me. I will always stand with you," Democratic nominee Angie Nixon, a state lawmaker from Jacksonville whose platform is considered DSA-aligned, wrote on X.

O’Brien also caught heat for voting in Florida, which appeared to signal a move from his hometown of Boston.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"Be union leader — move to a famously anti-union state — vote for a famously anti-union candidate — Brag about it — really cool stuff man," a top commenter on O’Brien’s post said. Other critics characterized O’Brien as a "scab", union jargon for someone who crosses a strike picket line to return to work for the company with which they are at odds.

The Teamsters leader’s announcement marked a noteworthy development with polls set to open nationwide in a matter of hours.

item.title: Talarico campaigns alongside Democrat who called ICE 'new KKK' and demanded its abolition
item.description: James Talarico praised Frederick Haynes III at a Texas rally, a congressional candidate who compared ICE to the KKK and called to abolish it.
item.content:encoded:
James Talarico, a U.S. Senate candidate in Texas, briefly praised Frederick Haynes III, a Democratic congressional candidate who compared President Donald Trump's immigration enforcement efforts to the KKK, at a get-out-the-vote event on Thursday as part of his Clear Eyes Full Hearts tour.

"Give it up for your next congressman Dr. Freddy Haynes. Thank you, Dr. Haynes, for those kind words and for your service to this community," Talarico said, following an introduction and speech from Haynes.

Although Talarico has not issued a formal endorsement of Haynes, the moment is notable for Talarico as he pitches himself as a Democrat who can represent the values of the Republican-leaning Lone Star State — and as he tries to distance himself from controversy over past remarks Republicans have characterized as woke.

TALARICO RALLY WARMUP ACT CALLS FOR ABOLISHING ICE, CONTRASTING SENATE HOPEFUL'S MESSAGE

Haynes, the pastor of Friendship-West Baptist Church, has framed many of his political views in the context of race and did so again on the event with Talarico.

"You transformed ICE into the new KKK and brought about terror in this nation," Haynes said of Trump's use of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

"It’s time to melt ICE. It’s time to abolish ICE," Haynes added.

Haynes is running to fill the seat of Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, the incumbent in Texas' 30th Congressional District who gave up her seat in a Senate bid she ultimately lost. During his campaign, Haynes has framed his support for climate policy as a fight against "environmental racism." He has also accused conservatives and the Trump administration of benefiting from fears of Black advancement.

"They have used Black people and perceived Black progress as the boogeyman. We have not witnessed this kind of corruption, this kind of blatant corruption," Haynes said in an October interview.

"We are witnessing the demolishing of what democratic infrastructure was built by the gains of the civil rights movement," Haynes added.

Even before his congressional run, Haynes made political commentary that relied heavily on a racial lens.

After the death of Charlie Kirk, a conservative political commentator who started Turning Point USA, Haynes described Kirk as a man with views "rooted in white supremacy" and contrasted it with the deaths of Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X.

"A White Christian gets killed, murdered — not assassinated. We going to tell the whole truth today. Martin King got assassinated. Malcolm X got assassinated. Medgar Evers got assassinated. Don’t compare Kirk to King," Haynes said in a September 2025 address to his church.

UN PUSHES NATIONS TO CONSIDER SLAVERY REPARATIONS BUT LEGAL GROUP SAYS IDEA 'NOT GOING TO FLY IN THE US'

Haynes would go on to condemn Kirk's death and political violence.

Haynes has also said he was a personal supporter of reparations.

"America, you owe us. What you done to us has been immoral. It’s been evil. It’s been unjust. It’s been downright wrong and the only way to bring salvation to America - you gotta pay us what you owe us," Haynes said at a Solidarity for Reparations event at a San Francisco church.

"I've come by to say, San Francisco, California, Texas, United States of America, if you want salvation to come to this house, you've got to engage in reparations."

For his own part, Talarico has also supported the idea of reparations, framing it as an outflow of his religious convictions.

"Reparations, repairing past harms, is part of my faith tradition. It’s part of the values I was raised with," Talarico said in a town hall meeting in July. "We have to correct the injustices of our past."

In the closing days of his campaign, Talarico has argued that, despite some of his views on race and gender which run counter to conservative stances, he could still represent Texas as a moderate.

TALARICO SAYS HE 'MISSED THE MARK' AS HE BACKTRACKS ON CONTROVERSIAL WOKE STATEMENTS

"Our campaign has been able to show that you can be a more moderate, reasonable candidate and still be exciting," Talarico said in October.

Talarico’s campaign did not respond to a request for comment if his comment about Haynes should be viewed as an endorsement of his platform or his views on race in politics.

item.title: Copilot killed in fiery Florida Learjet crash identified as 20-year-old who learned to fly before driving
item.description: Nathalia Gadelha, the 20-year-old copilot killed in the South Florida Learjet 60 crash, earned her private pilot license at 17.
item.content:encoded:
The copilot aboard a private jet that crashed into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday, killing all nine people on board, has been identified as a 20-year-old aspiring airline pilot who earned her wings before getting her driver's license, according to a report.

Nathalia Gadelha's mother and stepfather confirmed to the New York Post that she was the copilot aboard the Learjet 60 that plummeted into a residential area in Palm Beach County while traveling from Texas to the Bahamas.

Gadelha, who grew up in Palm Beach County, made headlines in 2023 when she earned her private pilot's license at just 17 years old while attending West Boca Raton High School.

DEADLY CRASH KILLS TWO AS PLANE PLUNGES INTO 'BALL OF FLAMES' NEAR SUBURBAN GOLF COURSE

"I definitely do brag because people say, 'Oh, you can't drive,' and I'm like, 'Yeah, but I can fly,'" she told local station CBS12 at the time.

Gadelha began taking flying lessons in 2020 and received additional instruction from her father, who had learned to fly recreationally in 2018, the outlet reported at the time.

The 2023 news report detailed how she accumulated 88 hours of flight time while pursuing her private pilot's license, which was funded through the School District of Palm Beach County's Aviation Academy.

The young aviator later graduated from American Flyers, a flight school based in Addison, Texas, with a location in Pompano Beach, Florida, according to the Post.

Gadelha told CBS12 that she hoped to become a commercial airline pilot.

In a recent social media post cited by the Post, she shared a video of herself flying with her boyfriend, Justin, highlighting their aviation accomplishments at such young ages.

"How often do you see 2 pilots under 21 with a commercial, multi-engine, instrument, CFI/CFI-I," she wrote, referring to several aviation certifications and instructor ratings.

The Learjet 60 departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas when it crashed near Cresthaven, Florida, around 12:50 p.m. Sunday, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.

All nine people aboard the aircraft were killed, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed Sunday afternoon.

4 FLORIDA FAMILY MEMBERS FOUND DEAD AFTER SMALL PLANE GOES DOWN OFF THE BAHAMAS

Air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net revealed that the flight crew reported ice accumulation and turbulence before the aircraft began rapidly losing altitude, according to The Associated Press.

"We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence," a pilot told controllers.

The crew subsequently requested permission to climb another 2,000 feet before declaring an emergency as the aircraft plunged toward the ground.

"We're descending 8,000 — mayday, mayday — we're descending 10,000 feet per minute," a pilot radioed, according to the AP.

"We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute," the pilot continued, before warning, "We're going to crash into the ground."

Dashcam footage captured the jet plunging nose-first into the neighborhood, as Fox News Digital previously reported.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis described the crash as "cataclysmic."

The crash also forced the evacuation of approximately 600 people from a nearby mobile home community, according to local officials.

The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the crash. The cause has not been determined, and NTSB officials are expected to provide an update Monday.

Fox News Digital’s Emma Bussey contributed to this report.

item.title: DOJ appeals to Supreme Court to reverse block on segregating 20K California ballots
item.description: The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to temporarily block rulings denying its bid to segregate over 20,000 California mail-in ballots.
item.content:encoded:
The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to temporarily block lower-court rulings that denied its request to segregate more than 20,000 California mail-in ballots cast by people it says are likely not U.S. citizens.

The DOJ argues the limited injunction would preserve the ballots while their eligibility is investigated, without canceling any votes. California and the federal government dispute whether the ballots are unlawful.

"Once illegally cast ballots are counted and commingled with lawful votes, the resulting harm is impossible to remedy," the Justice Department wrote in a court filing.

JUDGE REJECTS DOJ REQUEST TO BLOCK CALIFORNIA FROM IMMEDIATELY COUNTING BALLOTS LINKED TO ALLEGED NONCITIZENS

The 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the request Friday, with Judge Patrick Bumatay dissenting, as did a federal judge in Los Angeles last week. The case remains under review, and the DOJ is seeking relief while the matter proceeds. California says its safeguards against noncitizen voting are robust and argues the federal list may contain errors that could disenfranchise eligible voters. The lower courts also cited the state’s authority over election procedures and warned that granting the request could jeopardize the election.

DOJ HAS VERIFIED 20,000 NONCITIZENS ON CALIFORNIA VOTER ROLLS, FEDERAL PROSECUTOR SAYS

The case stems from an Oct. 15 Justice Department lawsuit alleging that California is impeding enforcement of a federal law barring noncitizens from voting in federal elections. The administration says the state violated the Constitution’s Supremacy Clause, which generally gives federal law precedence over state law.

The dispute comes amid the administration’s broader push to influence how states run elections, including demands for access to voter rolls and warnings that officials could face prosecution for knowingly allowing noncitizens to vote.

California, the nation’s most populous state, has 52 House seats. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to take control of the chamber.

Fox News' Shannon Bream and Bill Mears and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Mamdani, Hasan Piker among radical left-wing voices erupting over Haley Stevens' endorsement switch
item.description: Chuck Schumer, Hakeem Jeffries, and top Democrats unleashed fury at Haley Stevens after her endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers before Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Prominent Democrats and left-wing voices nationwide exploded with fury after Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in the final stretch of that state's U.S. Senate race in Michigan over the weekend.

In her video posted to social media on Sunday after attending church service with Rogers, Stevens noted how El-Sayed told her to "stay away" from his campaign and slammed him for embracing radical steamer Hasan Piker — who was among those criticizing the endorsement stunt.

"Working class people’s lives are on the ballot on Tuesday—their healthcare, their rent, their bills," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in an X post. "Haley Stevens just betrayed them by endorsing the very Republican she said she wanted to run against."

Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel said on X shortly after the endorsement: "Congresswoman Stevens is not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future."

EL SAYED'S LEFT-WING ALLIES ATTACK 'EVIL' STEVENS AFTER BOMBSHELL ROGERS ENDORSEMENT

Stevens, who will leave Congress in January, lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed earlier this year. She was widely viewed as the moderate, establishment candidate compared to the more progressive, left-wing policies of her opponent.

On Sunday, Stevens abandoned the party in the final hours of the Senate campaign as Democrats seek to win back control of the upper chamber.

"This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens," Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said on X. "Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors."

DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS ENDORSES GOP SENATE NOMINEE MIKE ROGERS AT DETROIT CHURCH

"Haley Stevens made a terrible decision, blindsided everyone and isolated herself from the House Democratic caucus," said House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y. "We will have a discussion about appropriate next steps upon our return."

Rep. Mark Pocan, D-Wis., called Stevens "clearly disturbed," and said she "has thrown her constituents under the bus" on several key midterm issues.

HALEY STEVENS RIPPED BY FELLOW DEMS FOR REFUSING TO EXPLICITLY BACK EL-SAYED: 'STAY THE F--- OFF TELEVISION'

"Too many people live off their 15 minutes of fame," Pocan continued. "In this case, she threw away an entire career because she couldn’t get over a loss and needed attention. Pathetic. Sad. Clearly she has some serious issues. But no one will take her seriously ever again."

Outside of her own colleagues condemning her endorsement, Stevens also saw an immediate staff exodus after she posted the video.

After the endorsement, a visibly upset El-Sayed demanded the media focus their questions on political issues, rather than Stevens' stunt.

EL-SAYED’S HASAN PIKER PROBLEM FOLLOWS HIM TO DEM CONVENTION AS JEWISH VOTERS BREAK RANKS

"I'm going to ask that when we take questions, you keep your questions focused on the issues that Michiganders really care about. Now that might not drive clicks for you. I get it. I understand your business, right? But they're the issues that Michiganders are paying attention to," he said.

FORMER RIVAL DODGES FULL-THROATED EL-SAYED ENDORSEMENT AFTER BITTER SENATE PRIMARY

Stevens drew an official condemnation from the Democratic Party at a national level, too.

"Haley Stevens’ disappointing decision to endorse Mike Rogers, a Trump ally who would join Republican efforts to sell out working families, is a betrayal of the values of the Democratic Party," Democratic National Committee (DNC) chairman Ken Martin said in a statement on behalf of the organization.

"At a moment when Democrats are united in fighting for Michigan families and standing up to Trump’s agenda, we reject these efforts to sow division within our party. We will not allow last-minute political stunts to derail our momentum and we will triple down on our efforts to elect Abdul El-Sayed on Tuesday."

The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), chaired by Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., lashed out at Stevens' decision, too.

MICHIGAN SENATE RIVALS CLASH OVER MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD ALLEGATIONS AS ROGERS DOUBLES DOWN ON EL-SAYED

"The stakes of this election could not be higher: Mike Rogers is a rubber stamp for Donald Trump, and together they plan to continue sowing chaos and making life unaffordable for families while prioritizing their billionaire donors at the expense of Michigan families," the DSCC statement said, adding the group will "reject any efforts to divide Democrats ahead of Tuesday’s crucial election."

DEMOCRAT RIPS HASAN PIKER AS 'HACK WHO THRIVES ON HATE' OVER HIS WARNING TO AMERICAN JEWS ABOUT ISRAEL

Piker, who was at the center of some of the reason Stevens' broke from El-Sayed, simply wrote: "i [sic] condemn haley stevens."

Piker has caused major controversy in the Michigan race due to his proximity to El-Sayed. Since his primary win, the progressive candidate has sought to distance himself from the streamer.

"This is the single most unproductive, selfish thing a Democratic candidate has done all cycle and likely many cycles before that," Pod Save America co-host and speechwriter to President Barack Obama said on X. "Having misjudged candidates in the past myself, I hope everyone who tried to recruit, support, and defend Haley can now admit what a mistake it was."

HALEY STEVENS URGES EL-SAYED TO DITCH HASAN PIKER AFFILIATION AFTER MICHIGAN PRIMARY

Fellow PodSaveAmerica cohost Jon Lovett called Stevens a "sleaze."

"Not to downplay Haley Stevens' vermin-like betrayal of her party and her constituents and her nation... But given her track record as a clownish loser, do we really believe any who will now follow her weren't already going to vote for the Fascist?" podcaster and former television sports personality Keith Olbermann said in an X post.

Stevens, who was narrowly defeated by El-Sayed in Michigan's Aug. 4, 2026 primary election, crossed partisan lines after saying for months that she would support El-Sayed.

It all devolved after Stevens expressed concern last week over an ad aired in El-Sayed's favor that was widely viewed as antisemitic. She said she would appear at a weekend campaign event with El-Sayed on the condition that he denounced the ad. El-Sayed, whose support among the Michigan Jewish community is already tenuous, disinvited her from the event instead.

The ad that sparked the controversy was released by the Rebellion PAC, which is operated by The Young Turks co-founder and bombastic leftist commentator Cenk Uygur, who is Piker's uncle. Piker, whom El-Sayed invited onto the campaign trail in Michigan during primary season, has been a headache for El-Sayed during the general election.

Piker said in 2019 that "America deserved 9/11." He has also praised Mao Zedong and Communist China, said capitalists should be murdered in the streets and is known for making antisemitic comments.

El-Sayed has refused to denounce Piker, brushing him off as a "streamer from California" who he says shouldn't be the focus of the campaign in Michigan.

item.title: Judge tosses case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying to Congress about Hunter Biden investigation
item.description: A federal judge dismissed the case against two FBI officials in the Hunter Biden probe, accusing Trump and Kash Patel of directing a "rush job."
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge tossed criminal charges against two former FBI officials accused of lying to Congress about the Hunter Biden investigation Monday, delivering a blistering rebuke of the prosecution and accusing the Trump administration's Justice Department of weaponizing the justice system.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui dismissed the criminal complaint against former FBI officials Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides from the bench, sharply criticizing the government's handling of the prosecution.

"What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization," Faruqui said, describing the case as a "rush job" directed by President Donald Trump and FBI Director Kash Patel.

The case stemmed from allegations that the officials lied to Congress about their knowledge of Hunter Biden’s laptop and the bureau’s handling of investigations involving him ahead of the 2020 presidential election.

EX-FBI OFFICIALS ARRESTED IN HUNTER BIDEN LAPTOP PROBE AS TESTIMONY COMES UNDER SCRUTINY

The ruling capped a series of hearings in which Faruqui questioned the government's decision to pursue the case through a criminal complaint rather than a grand jury indictment and blasted prosecutors for attempting to add another charge without first securing judicial approval.

Republicans have long accused the FBI of improperly handling information about Hunter Biden ahead of the 2020 presidential election, alleging that political bias influenced the bureau's decisions.

Prosecutors alleged that Floris and Benavides made false statements during congressional interviews in 2023 about what they knew and did that were contradicted by internal FBI communications and witness accounts.

During a preliminary hearing last week, Faruqui blasted prosecutors for filing an unsigned, unsworn criminal complaint seeking to add obstruction charges without first obtaining judicial approval.

Faruqui struck the revised complaint from the record, forcing prosecutors to proceed on their original allegations that the former officials lied to Congress.

FBI CO-DEPUTY DIRECTOR ANDREW BAILEY RESIGNS AFTER YEAR IN ROLE

The judge questioned why prosecutors had bypassed standard procedures, while defense attorneys pointed out that the revised complaint also softened the government's original allegations about the officials' involvement in Hunter Biden investigations. 

Faruqui, who was appointed a U.S. magistrate judge in 2020, has previously sharply criticized federal prosecutors handling cases under the Trump administration.

He apologized to the suspect accused of plotting an assassination attempt against Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner.

JUDGE WHO APOLOGIZED TO ACCUSED WOULD-BE TRUMP ASSASSIN LIGHTS UP DOJ IN HUNTER BIDEN FBI CASE

"To me, it’s extremely disturbing that he was put in five-point restraints, a person with no criminal history. It’s troubling," said Faruqui, referring to suspect Cole Allen's jail treatment in May. "I never heard of one Jan. 6 defendant who was put in five-point restraints or in a safe cell. If the only way to keep him safe is the most punitive thing, that’s a problem."

Faruqui also previously clashed with federal prosecutors in Washington over Trump administration law-enforcement surge cases, accusing U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro’s office of overreaching by bringing some matters in federal court that he said belonged in local court.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and FBI for comment.

Fox News' Jake Gibson contributed to this report.

item.title: Christa Pike's execution doctor says misplaced IV sent lethal drugs into her arms instead of veins
item.description: Dr. Mark Fowler reveals an improperly placed IV sent pentobarbital into Christa Pike's tissue instead of her bloodstream during the failed execution.
item.content:encoded:
The doctor who participated in Christa Pike's failed execution in Tennessee says an improperly placed IV sent lethal drugs into the tissue of her arms instead of her bloodstream — and acknowledged the execution team should have stopped when the death row inmate complained of pain.

Dr. Mark Fowler, who served as the physician during Pike's Sept. 30 execution attempt, offered a rare firsthand account of what went wrong in an interview with New York Magazine published Friday.

Pike, 50, survived after receiving two doses of pentobarbital and was hospitalized for days before eventually regaining consciousness.

TENNESSEE DEATH ROW INMATE SURVIVES 2 LETHAL INJECTION DOSES IN FAILED EXECUTION ATTEMPT

The doctor told the magazine he knew something was wrong when Pike's execution stretched to about 45 minutes. When he was called into the chamber, she was still alive and gasping for air.

Fowler said he initially considered whether Pike's response to the medication could simply be taking longer than expected and decided to give it more time.

DEATH ROW INMATE UNCONSCIOUS ON VENTILATOR AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION FOR TEEN’S KILLING: ATTORNEYS

As another half-hour passed, he became concerned that Pike could survive with irreversible brain damage. Fowler later diagnosed her as comatose before a deputy commissioner ordered the execution stopped.

He then ordered oxygen, and Pike was taken by ambulance to Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

911 OPERATORS QUESTIONED WHETHER CHRISTA PIKE FAILED EXECUTION CALL WAS PRANK, AUDIO REVEALS

Fowler told New York Magazine that the IV used to administer the pentobarbital had not been properly inserted into Pike's veins.

"It was delivering medicine to the subcutaneous tissue" of her arms, Fowler said.

DEATH ROW KILLER CHRISTA PIKE DESCRIBES WAKING UP AFTER EXECUTION SHE NEVER EXPECTED TO SURVIVE

Pike's attorneys previously said in a court filing that she complained of severe arm pain during the execution, telling those in the chamber, "My arm feels like it’s about to burst open."

"They should have stopped and reassessed, and they didn’t," Fowler told New York Magazine.

item.title: 'Homestead' star Bailey Chase says California vaccine plans were 'final straw' that drove family out of LA
item.description: Bailey Chase reveals the proposed COVID-19 vaccine mandate that drove his family from California to the mountains of North Carolina five years ago.
item.content:encoded:
"Homestead" star Bailey Chase is opening up about the "final straw" that drove him and his family out of California for a new life in North Carolina.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old actor, who shares daughter Waverly, 12, and 10-year-old twins Maggie and Gauge with his wife Amy, explained that concerns over how California's COVID-19 restrictions would impact his children led him to leave the Golden State behind.

"That happened five years ago in the throes of COVID," Chase said. "My wife and I picked up sticks with our three young children when they were mandating vaccines out there."

"They said they couldn't go back to school without it," Chase, who stars as former Green Beret Jeff Eriksson in "Homestead," continued. "And that was the final straw. And we've been in the mountains of North Carolina ever since living our best life."

ZACHARY LEVI SAYS TEXAS GIVES HIM THE ‘FREEDOM’ HE COULDN’T FIND IN CALIFORNIA

Five years after trading Los Angeles for North Carolina, Chase told Fox News Digital that his life now largely revolves around his children's activities when he isn't working.

'VIRGIN RIVER' STAR BEN HOLLINGSWORTH SAYS HIS KIDS HAVE FREEDOM IN SMALL TOWN THAT 'DOESN'T FLY' IN LA

"I'm like soccer dad right now. It's soccer season, so we're going here and there," he said. "My oldest is really into ballet, and I couldn't be more proud of her and getting ready for ‘The Nutcracker’ in December, and basketball season's around the corner."

While Chase remains committed to his acting career, the "Longmire" alum said his priorities shift completely when he returns home.

CHRIS PRATT SAYS HIS FAITH WILL BE 'THE MOST IMPORTANT THING' THAT HE PASSES ON TO HIS KIDS

"I love my job, and when I'm off filming, I'm 100% focused on that. But when I'm home, I'm home," he said. "There's no greater job than being a dad."

Chase and his family currently live in Amy's hometown of Hendersonville in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Western North Carolina, about 25 miles south of Asheville. Chase has previously explained that Amy had long envisioned eventually returning to the area where she was born and raised. The actor also has ties to North Carolina after attending Duke University in Durham on a football scholarship.

'RANSOM CANYON' STAR JOSH DUHAMEL SAYS HE'D RATHER PUT MONEY INTO NORTH DAKOTA AFTER SELLING LOS ANGELES HOME

"Amy, being from the mountains of North Carolina, always had it in the back of her mind that she’d go back home one day," he said in a January 2026 interview with Duke Alumni Magazine. "We didn’t know how or when."

However, Chase recalled they decided the time was right due to California's handling of the pandemic.

‘TWILIGHT’ STAR KELLAN LUTZ TRADED CALIFORNIA FOR TENNESSEE LAND AND BIBLE STUDIES

"Things started to not work in LA during COVID – they shut down the schools, there were no sports for the kids," he said. "Really, no life, no work. And it became more and more obvious that we should leave LA."

"Amy’s very close with her parents, who are in N.C.," he continued. "Everything’s about seven minutes away: school, the in-laws, the grocery store, golf course, soccer field. It’s a great location. We live in a house that would not have been affordable in LA."

JANA KRAMER SAYS LOS ANGELES PRICED HER OUT OF THE CHILDHOOD SHE WANTED FOR HER KIDS

"It’s a kid’s dream," he added. "There’s a sports court and a pool. We have two golden retriever puppies, so it’s a full and lively house."

During a February appearance on the "Undaunted.Life: A Man's Podcast," Chase elaborated on the concerns that he had over California's proposed vaccine mandate for his young children's return to school.

"At that time, you know, they're 4, 4 and 6 years old," he recalled. "I got two young girls and, you know we don't need to go down that rabbit hole."

"I was like, 'No, I just don't know enough,'" he continued. "And I got one job right now, and it's to take care of these little nuggets. That's the most important job I have right now."

In October 2021, California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced plans for a COVID-19 vaccine requirement for students that he said would eventually apply to all the state's 6.7 million public and private schoolchildren.

However, the mandate was repeatedly delayed and ultimately never took effect. In February 2023, state health officials announced that they would not pursue or implement the requirement as the COVID-19 state of emergency expired at the end of that month. 

'ANT-MAN' STAR EVANGELINE LILLY SAYS SHE LEFT HOLLYWOOD BECAUSE SHE 'ALWAYS HATED BEING FAMOUS'

Chase previously acknowledged that while relocating to North Carolina was the best move for his family, leaving LA came at a professional cost after he spent 21 years building his career in Hollywood.

"I've lost out on some work by not being in L.A.," he admitted while appearing on the "Living Local" podcast in August.

"There was a big role on 'Grey's Anatomy,'" he continued. "And I understand, it's a lot cheaper for them. They just move on to the next guy and cast someone who's local to L.A."

"But what has happened is I've gotten new opportunities and different kind of jobs and some faith-based films and shows," Chase added.

The "Saving Grace" actor has also spoken openly about how he "lost touch" with God during his years in LA and shared that moving to North Carolina eventually led him back to his Christian faith.

"Moving back here, I've gotten reconnected to my faith," Chase told "Crosswalk" in January. "Just started going to church recently. It took a few years, but I really like the church where we're going to here."

"My cousin started taking us," he continued. "The girls are in youth group. They really love it."

"It's nice to be in an environment where I can openly talk about God and Jesus and without fear of criticism," he added.

WATCH HERE: ‘HOMESTEAD’ STAR BAILEY CHASE SAYS CALIFORNIA VACCINE PLANS WERE ‘FINAL STRAW’ THAT DROVE FAMILY OUT OF LA

In a 2024 Instagram post, Chase reflected on how his priorities have shifted since leaving behind "all that worry, all that stress, 20 years of hustle in LA."

"It also got me thinking if I spent as much time chasing God as I’ve spent chasing success the last 25 years, what would that look like?" he wrote.

Chase is currently starring as former Green Beret Jeff Eriksson in the faith-based streaming platform Angel Studios’ post-apocalyptic drama "Homestead," which will premiere its second season on Nov. 3. 

The series follows survivors living at a fortified prepper compound in the Rocky Mountains known as The Homestead after a nuclear attack on LA plunges the country into chaos. After the bomb is detonated, Jeff escapes with his family to The Homestead, where he serves as head of security.

The actor starred in the 2024 theatrical movie "Homestead," which introduces the story and the TV series picks up directly afterward. The cast also includes Neal McDonough, Kevin Lawson Emmanuel McCord, Jesse Hutch, Betzaida Landín, Charles Esten and Dawn Olivieri.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Chase told Fox News Digital that starring in the "Homestead" movie and follow-up TV show had inspired the cast to start prepping for a potential apocalypse.

"'Homestead' has changed all of our lives and the first thing I did when I came home after the film was arm my home more," he said. "And then right before season two, Hurricane Helene hit here in the mountains of North Carolina. And I now have a brand-new generator and some other things."

When asked if most Americans would be able to survive a major disaster, Chase predicted that it would be more challenging for people who live in bigger cities.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"They're overpopulated and there aren't enough resources," he said. "So for those who are a little bit more in the country, their odds are a lot higher."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Those are the kind of people who hunt and fish and can go out and find their own game," Chase added. "So if I'm laying odds, I'm betting on those guys."

While reflecting on what drew him to "Homestead," Chase explained that his focus on faith and family has also influenced the projects he chooses, noting that the show offers a different message than much of what is coming out of Hollywood.

"I take my job as being a father as the best job and most important job that I'll ever have. And I do take it seriously," Chase told Fox News Digital.

"And how that translates to me being an actor, that's why I'm so proud of ‘Homestead’ and the story that we get to tell, because it reflects my own personal values," he continued. "We got men and women and boys and girls, and it's about promoting faith, family, community and being there for your brother."

"Not all the shows that Hollywood's putting out does that, so I feel truly blessed to be part of a show that delivers a message that I believe in so deeply to my core."

"Homestead: The Series" season two premieres Nov. 3 on Angel with new episodes released weekly on Tuesdays.

item.title: DR ANNIE ANDREWS: South Carolina should expect more from their senator
item.description: Dr. Annie Andrews details her Taxpayer Pledge, vowing to ban stock trading, end congressional pensions and make no tax on tips permanent.
item.content:encoded:
Throughout this race, I’ve said it plainly: whether you voted for Donald Trump, Lindsey Graham, or anyone else, if you care more about your bills than Washington’s political games, this campaign is for you.

I mean it. Last week in Aiken, I stood in a room full of Republicans and independents. One man told me he’d been a Reagan Republican his whole life and had never voted for a Democrat. He came anyway. He wanted to know if I’d actually listen.

I’ve been listening for 18 months on the campaign trail, and for 20 years before that in my exam room.

INDEPENDENT VOTERS AREN’T PICKING A POLITICAL TEAM, THEY JUST FEEL PICKED ON

I didn’t set out to become a politician. I’m a pediatrician and a mom of three. I’ve cared for children whose parents had to choose between groceries and an inhaler, and I’ve taken the 2 a.m. calls from scared moms and dads. Medicine taught me that you show up, you listen, and you make hard decisions under pressure.

I’ve traveled to all 46 counties. In Barnwell, I sat on the back of a pickup truck with eighth-generation farmers hurt by tariffs. In Ridgeland, I stood with veterans who have lost friends to suicide and want this war in Iran to end. In Marlboro County, I met a little boy growing up without a hospital because of where he lives. In Myrtle Beach, a 26-year Marine veteran and lifelong Republican came to one of our events after someone encouraged him to attend. Afterward, he told me he’d just made his first political donation.

When I ask when they last saw a senator in their hometown, they laugh. They deserve better.

This week, Fox News moved our race to a toss-up. Former Republican Gov. David Beasley endorsed me, and more than 100 South Carolina Republican leaders have joined our campaign. They don’t agree with me on everything, but they know I’ll put South Carolina ahead of any party or special interest.

My opponent, Darline Graham, has my deepest sympathy for the loss of her brother. But a Senate seat isn’t an inheritance. She was handpicked by Washington insiders, and she has admitted she’s "not that informed" on national security while our country is at war. South Carolinians deserve a senator who’s ready.

Here’s my commitment: I’ll be an independent voice and a brick wall between South Carolina and Washington, even when my own party gets it wrong. Democrats spend billions without asking whether programs work. Republicans waste billions on endless wars and corporate handouts. Our debt just hit $40 trillion.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

My Taxpayer Pledge starts with Congress: ban members from trading stocks, end their taxpayer-funded pensions and stop their pay during shutdowns. I’ll oppose tax increases on families making under $500,000, make No Tax on Tips and No Tax on Social Security permanent, and end special tax breaks for data centers.

I’ve pledged to serve no more than two terms, because this seat doesn’t belong to one family or one party. It belongs to you. If I don’t keep my word, fire me in six years.

I’m asking South Carolina to hire a senator who will show up, listen and get to work for you.

item.title: Haley Stevens' endorsement stunt backfires with El-Sayed setting single-day fundraising record
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's campaign reports a $2.4 million single-day fundraising surge after Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign says it raised more than $2.4 million in a single day, setting a fundraising record in the final stretch of the Michigan race.

The Democratic candidate's campaign said Sunday’s haul came from more than 65,000 donors, who gave an average of $36.74. Nearly 29,600 people contributed to the campaign for the first time.

The fundraising surge came on the heels of Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., endorsing Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday after months of turmoil following her primary loss to the more progressive candidate.

DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS ENDORSES GOP SENATE NOMINEE MIKE ROGERS

"As Michiganders head to the polls, the momentum behind Abdul’s campaign has never been stronger," campaign spokesperson Cole Wozniak said in a statement following the final-hour cash haul.

Stevens, who was considered the more moderate establishment candidate in her primary against El-Sayed earlier this year, said she remains "a very proud Democrat" who loves Michigan.

She insisted, however, in the video message posted to social media over the weekend that she could not support El-Sayed, citing his backing from radical left-wing political streamer Hasan Piker.

"Hey Michigan, as you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul said that I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away and he's right. And that's why I'm endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today," Stevens said in a video posted on X.

The endorsement of the Trump-backed Republican candidate drew swift criticism from Democrats.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called it "a despicable betrayal" and said his caucus in the upper chamber remains united behind El-Sayed.

Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel also condemned Stevens’ decision, saying she had "abandoned everything she claims to care about."

El-Sayed brushed off the endorsement Sunday, telling reporters he does not think about Stevens or Rogers and was focused on voters and policy.

He also has attempted in recent months to distance himself from Piker amid the streamer's rising national recognition and increased scrutiny on his controversial statements — including antisemitic sentiments and claiming that "America deserved 9/11."

item.title: Andrew Novak cruises in Mexico, the Blades Brown knighting rumor, and Fifa Laopakdee heads back to the Masters
item.description: Andrew Novak shot 61-62 across 36 holes to claim a five-shot victory at the Mexico Open, while a wild Blades Brown rumor stole the spotlight.
item.content:encoded:
This year's Mexico Open did not deliver the same incredible level of drama we witnessed at Vidanta Vallarta a year ago, thanks to Andrew Novak transforming into prime Tiger Woods, but you can't complain about a guy going on an absolute heater en route to his first individual title on the PGA Tour.

Blades Brown was in the field in Mexico and finished a respectable T-19, and during the event, an unsubstantiated yet absolutely hysterical rumor about the teenage phenom made the rounds in the golf world. It involves actual swords, knighting, and meetings around a round table.

In New Zealand, our eyes were fortunate enough to get a look at Te Arai Links for the Asia-Pacific Amateur. While the golf course was the main character, looking like a piece of land that could only be found on a planet not named Earth, Fifa Laopakdee went back-to-back, earning a Masters invite for the second consecutive year.

Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com.

Andrew Novak was in the midst of a lackluster 2026 season before arriving in Mexico. The Wofford College grad missed the cut in three of the four majors, didn't play the weekend at The Players, and managed just two Top 10s in 25 starts if you excluded the team event Zurich Classic.

To say something clicked at the Mexico Open would be disrespectful to his performance.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

After an opening round 67 put him five shots back of the lead, he woke up on Friday and decided that over the next 36 holes he was going to turn into the best putter on the property and essentially not miss a thing.

Novak led the field in strokes gained: putting in both rounds two and three, picking up over 5.6 shots on the greens alone on Friday, posting scores of 61-62. When you shoot 19-under across 36 holes as Novak did, you're going to separate from the field, which is exactly what happened before ultimately earning a five-shot victory.

Steven Fisk and Kristoffer Ventura both shot final rounds of 63 only to lose by five. That has to be quite the feeling.

Novak, who won the 2025 Zurich Classic alongside teammate Ben Griffin, moves up to 53rd in the FedEx Cup Fall standings. Finishing inside the Top 50 is huge, with those players earning spots in full-field and signature events in 2027.

When your first name is Blades, you're destined to play golf at some level. Blades Brown just so happens to ooze so much talent that he decided to skip out on college, turn professional as a teenager, and earn his PGA Tour card before turning 20.

In order to get to the level Brown has climbed to in such fast fashion, one has to have a team around them, and young Mr. Blades allegedly takes the formation of said team very, very seriously.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK GOLF COVERAGE

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Andy Johnson of The Fried Egg has heard a rumor involving Brown and his team, and it may be the greatest thing my 33-year-old ears have ever heard.

During an episode of The Shotgun Start podcast last week, Johnson emphasized that the rumor is unsubstantiated, but that doesn't make it any less incredible.

"Everybody has their teams and everything in golf, your trainer, coaches, your agents, your parents, and I'm hearing that Blades has an interesting aspect to his team," Johnson began. "In order to become a part of the team, you have to get knighted, and you're given a sword. So everyone on his team, whether it's his swing coach, his personal trainer, his agent, they have swords, and they commence and discuss Blades Brown business around a round table.

"Mike Sposa is his equipment guy for Callaway, and he was given a sword, and you become knighted to become part of Blades' team."

item.title: NASCAR's new villain picks another victim and fans want him parked, driver flies with Trump & ratings rebound?
item.description: Carson Hocevar's four brake checks on Austin Cindric at Martinsville stunned NASCAR drivers and fans alike heading into the Homestead finale.
item.content:encoded:
Monday Morning Pit-Stop is a weekly NASCAR column that runs on OutKick.com and Fox News Digital. If you're looking for a normal NASCAR recap, go check out insufferable ESPN ... assuming they still know NASCAR exists.

And then there was one.

That's right. One race left in this 2026 NASCAR season. Hard to believe. Feels like we just revved engines in Daytona, and now we're taking the checkered flag about 300 miles south in Homestead.

It flew by!

Not really.

Sometimes, it does. Not this year. This NASCAR season has felt like a grind, hasn't it? Some of it was good. Some of it was bad. Some of it was really, really sad.

CHASE ELLIOTT SAYS NASCAR'S GRUELING 10-MONTH SEASON CAN 'EAT YOU UP' WITHOUT AN ESCAPE

It's just been a grind.

But that's a topic for next week, when we begin our two months of offseason decompression. For now, we leave Martinsville with everyone pissed at the same dude they've been pissed at all season long ...

Carson Hocevar! In a shocking turn of events, Carson made more enemies on the track yesterday, and I'm not sure even I can defend him this time. I've generally tried to defend Carson most of the season because A) I think he's good for the sport, and B) he's definitely good for this column, but I think he probably deserves whatever he's got coming to him after yesterday.

You'll see.

What else? I've got a nice little ratings rebound at 'Dega after the Phoenix disaster (sort of), Kyle Larson could have the championship wrapped up before the sun goes down next Sunday, and Austin Dillon boards Air Force One with Trump and heads to Daytona.

There are worse ways to spend a Friday, I reckon.

NASCAR'S MOST HATED DRIVER ATTACKED AGAIN, ATTACKER'S WIFE GIVES THE DOUBLE-BIRD & WHY DID THE SPORT DIE?

Four tires, a quick splash of that Sunoco racing fuel, and maybe some brake fluid for Carson Hocevar ... Monday Morning Pit-Stop — the 'Brake Check 1, 2, 3' edition' — is LIVE!

Let's go ahead and congratulate William Byron right off the bat so we can move on to more exciting things.

Byron led a billion laps (362) on his way to absolutely destroying the field yesterday at Martinsville. It was his first win of the season. Chase Elliott finished second. Kyle Larson finished ninth, and now heads to Homestead basically needing to finish the race to win another championship.

Probably won't be quite as exciting as the old Championship Four races, but everyone was so appalled at Joey Logano winning that one time that we got that taken away from us and now we get this.

Oh well.

Anyway, it was a good day for Hendrick Motorsports. Was it the most exciting Martinsville race ever? Lord no. Again, William Byron led 362 (!!!) laps. There wasn't exactly that usual Martinsville drama ...

At the front of the pack.

At the back of it, though? Where Carson Hocevar found himself locked in a tight battle with Austin Cindric?

Yeah, buddy, there was drama:

Amazing. Look, I can't even defend it. That was so hilariously obvious from Carson Hocevar, I don't even know what to say.

He can sit there and feed us the BS "It's just Martinsville" line, but that doesn't quite work in the days of SMT data and instant replay. Not one, not two, not three, but FOUR brake checks before he finally destroyed the No. 2 car.

Just nasty work from Carson. Nasty, nasty work. Austin Cindric, by the way, declined the NBC interview after the race. I'd imagine that means he's keeping his options on the table for next weekend's finale and doesn't want to tip his hand to NASCAR.

Just a guess.

And by the way, for those calling me a drama queen for not siding with Carson here ...

I present to you Kenny Wallace:

"Holyeeee s–t!! I’ve never witnessed anything like this," Wallace tweeted Sunday.

No? Still not good enough for you?

How about Corey LaJoie?

"Good God Almighty," he said.

Two NASCAR drivers — one former, one current — both appalled at whatever the hell that was from Carson Hocevar. And I like Carson! I've defended him a ton this year. I think NASCAR desperately needs a villain, and I think he fills that role nicely.

But Lordy, this was a bad look. Even his own spotter was tired of it yesterday:

"Hey just go. Please? Just go."

Like I said at the jump — it's been a long season. You can hear it in Tyler Green's voice. Don't blame him.

As for the fans ... they weren't pleased, either.

Let's take a look:

So, there are a ton of fans calling for NASCAR to "park" Carson Hocevar. Feel like that's a bit silly. There's one race left. Feel like this is a spot where NASCAR can let the drivers work it out on the track, no? Who's gonna get in line first next week at Homestead to wreck Carson Hocevar?

Austin Cindric? Ryan Blaney? Brad Keselowski? Zane Smith? He's made so many enemies this year, I've lost count.

Head on a swivel when you get down here, Carson!

OK, let's put the pedal to the floor and get to a couple quickies on the way out. First up?

Last week, we talked about NASCAR's horrific ratings for the Phoenix race a few weeks back (1.2 million). It was awful. I said the folks in marketing should be alarmed by what they saw. Lord knows I was.

For what it's worth, I do have it on good authority that those folks in NASCAR HQ are NOT worried about the number. They believe it's been a decent season, and feel the numbers have been a little off due to Nielsen reporting things a little differently. That's true, by the way.

Nielsen has changed its methodology in reporting. We don't have time to get into it today, but there is some truth to that.

Anyway — as expected — a shift back to NBC and to Talladega got things somewhat back on track last week:

Not bad! 2.5 million. Up 1% from last year. Down from the 3.1 in 2024. On par with everything else the past five years.

Look, it's fine. I'm sure NASCAR was thrilled to get that number back in the 2s. It was the highest-rated race since the season finale at Daytona in August.

Again, though, it was also back on NBC for the first time in months. Network TV was expected to give the Cup Series a much-needed boost, and it delivered. We'll see what Martinsville looks like.

Next? Before we head on out, let's all hop aboard Air Force One with Austin Dillon and get this election week started right!

"Air Force One with Pop Pop. God Bless the USA," Dillon wrote on Instagram.

Pop Pop, for those who couldn't piece it together, is Richard Childress. Those two accompanied Trump to his Daytona rally last Friday. I'm sure liberals handled it well!

In other news ... this election season ends in, like, 36 hours.

Amen. I can't wait.

OK, that's it for today. Good start to November. One race left, folks. Let's dial it in for one more race.

On the way out, here's NASCAR driver Natalie Decker attending a horse race over the weekend.

Giddy-up.

item.title: LEE CARTER: The 5 words that explain this election better than any commercial
item.description: Affordability, socialism, corruption, Trump and turnout: five words a researcher says explain the 2026 midterms better than $11 billion in ads.
item.content:encoded:
Eleven billion dollars.

Actually, more than that. Political advertising spending and reservations have now exceeded $11.6 billion, making this the most expensive election cycle for political advertising in American history.

For that kind of money, you'd think somebody might have figured out how to make groceries cheaper.

MIDTERMS UNLEASH WHAT MAY BE THE NASTIEST BARRAGE OF ATTACK ADS YET

Instead, Americans have endured months of attack ads, apocalyptic warnings and politicians insisting that civilization itself is on the ballot. Again.

As a researcher, I've spent much of this year studying what Americans believe, what frustrates them and, perhaps most importantly, what might motivate them to vote.

And I've become convinced that five words explain this election better than a thousand campaign commercials.

Affordability. Socialism. Corruption. Trump. Turnout.

Each tells us something about the American electorate. Together, they reveal something neither party should find particularly comforting.

Americans may be less interested in voting for somebody than in voting against something.

INDEPENDENT VOTERS AREN’T PICKING A POLITICAL TEAM, THEY JUST FEEL PICKED ON

And the two parties are betting on very different fears.

AFFORDABILITY

Washington has a remarkable talent for telling Americans how well they're doing while Americans are busy wondering how they're going to pay for everything.

Inflation is cooling! The stock market is booming! Economic growth is strong!

Wonderful.

Now explain why a family of four needs a financing plan to buy groceries and a second job to take everyone to Disney World.

Here's what politicians keep missing: Americans don't experience the economy as a collection of statistics. They experience it as a series of small humiliations.

FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS

Putting something back on the grocery shelf. Declining a dinner invitation. Explaining to your child why the family vacation will have to wait another year.

The economy isn't what Washington says is happening. It's what Americans can afford to do.

Republicans have spent much of this campaign telling voters that things are getting better. Democrats have spent it reminding them how expensive everything remains.

The Democrats have the easier argument.

But there's a catch.

Convincing voters that Republicans haven't made their lives better is not the same as convincing them that Democrats will.

One requires an attack ad. The other requires an actual plan.

SOCIALISM

For years, Republicans have warned that Democrats are taking America toward socialism. The accusation has been deployed so enthusiastically that you'd think Karl Marx was running for Congress in every competitive district.

Democrats often dismiss it as tired political fearmongering.

They may be making a serious mistake.

In polling I've been examining, the share of Republicans energized to vote against socialism has climbed from 50% to 59% in just a month.

Think about what that means.

Republicans can be disappointed in their candidates, frustrated with the economy and unhappy with their party's performance while remaining extraordinarily motivated to vote.

Why?

Because they may believe the alternative is worse.

Disappointment makes people complain. Fear makes them act.

Democrats see socialism as an outdated Republican talking point. Many Republicans see it as a threat to the country they love.

That doesn't mean Republicans are necessarily happy with their own party.

It means they may be willing to vote for a party they don't particularly like to stop one they fear even more.

And that's a potentially powerful turnout strategy hiding in plain sight.

CORRUPTION

Remember when draining the swamp was a campaign promise?

Apparently, the swamp has become a bipartisan swimming pool.

According to research from the Brennan Center and Wesleyan Media Project, nearly one-third of congressional television ads this cycle have referenced government ethics or campaign finance.

Americans increasingly suspect that the people running the country are playing by an entirely different set of rules.

Democrats have eagerly made corruption a central attack against Republicans.

But they should be careful about throwing stones from inside their own rather expensive glass houses.

Consider Alaska, where reports that Democratic-aligned operatives helped recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan have sparked allegations of election manipulation. Democrat Mary Peltola has denied knowing about the effort.

Whatever the ultimate findings, the controversy is a reminder that political hardball doesn't have a party registration.

But there's something deeper happening here.

When Americans are working harder and getting less while politicians and well-connected insiders somehow keep getting richer, every economic frustration begins to look like evidence of a rigged system.

The grocery bill isn't simply too high. Someone must be benefiting.

Healthcare isn't simply too expensive. Someone must be gaming the system.

You can convince voters that your opponent is corrupt without convincing them that you're honest.

And when voters believe everybody is playing dirty, the winner may inherit the office without inheriting much public confidence.

TRUMP

Donald Trump isn't running for Congress.

You'd never know it.

He's crisscrossing the country, dominating headlines and rallying supporters as though his own name were printed at the top of every ballot.

And he may understand something that the conventional election narrative is missing.

Trump's national approval ratings are weak. His base, however, remains intensely loyal.

Those aren't contradictory facts.

They're the defining feature of his political appeal.

Democrats have spent more than $163 million on advertising mentioning Trump since September 1, compared with roughly $11 million by Republicans.

Apparently, the Democratic Party's most valuable campaign surrogate is the Republican president.

But Trump has an advantage of his own.

Many of his supporters aren't Republicans who happen to like Trump.

They're Trump supporters who happen to vote Republican.

And those voters don't always show up when he isn't running.

Which may explain why he's campaigning as though he is.

His supporters may not feel particularly inspired to save the Republican Party. But they might be motivated to save Donald Trump from a Democratic Congress.

Democrats want this election to be a referendum on Trump.

Trump wants it to be a referendum on whether his supporters will defend him.

Both sides are making the same man the center of the election.

They're just hoping voters respond in opposite ways.

TURNOUT

And that brings us to the word that could determine everything.

Turnout.

The polls tell a remarkably consistent story. Democrats have an advantage. Economic frustration is widespread. The president is unpopular.

But elections aren't simply a measure of public opinion.

They're a measure of who participates.

As a researcher, I believe deeply in what polling can tell us. We can measure attitudes, identify motivations and model which voters are likely to show up.

But there's a reason we call them likely voters.

The most consequential difference in an election isn't always between Republicans and Democrats. It's between people who are angry enough to vote and people who are exhausted enough to stay home.

Democrats are angry about what Republicans have done.

Republicans may be frightened by what they believe Democrats will do.

Independents may be frustrated with both.

And that creates a fascinating question.

Which emotion will actually get people out of the house?

Gallup recently found that 56% of Americans have given considerable thought to this election, a record for this point in a midterm cycle.

But paying attention and participating aren't the same thing.

A wave of Democratic enthusiasm in safely blue districts won't change control of Congress. A smaller Republican surge in a handful of competitive races could.

And a relatively modest number of independents deciding to stay home or to show up could rewrite the headlines.

The polls can tell us where voters stand.

Tuesday will tell us which voters stand up.

And that distinction could determine the election.

Here's what I suspect both parties will get wrong once the votes are counted.

If Democrats win big, they'll declare that America has rejected Trumpism and embraced their vision.

If Republicans outperform expectations, they'll insist voters have reaffirmed the president's agenda.

Both may be mistaking a victory for an endorsement.

Voters can fire one party without falling in love with the other.

And they can stick with a party they don't particularly like because they're more afraid of the alternative.

That's the paradox of American politics in 2026.

We have two parties desperately trying to win an election in a country increasingly skeptical that either deserves to.

After more than $11 billion in political advertising, thousands of polls and enough promises to wallpaper the Capitol, Americans may be sending a remarkably simple message.

They don't want politicians to win another argument.

They want someone to make their lives better.

Tuesday will tell us who wins power.

What happens afterward will tell us whether they deserved it.

item.title: Lions coach leads locker room prayer for Jack Campbell after linebacker hospitalized with neck injury

Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell remained hospitalized overnight after suffering a serious neck injury during the team’s Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

Campbell went down on the turf at Ford Field and was not moving after hitting Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. He was placed on a backboard and carted off the field in the fourth quarter in the team’s 19-15 win. His teammates were in tears as he was being helped off the ground.

"So, here’s what I wanna do, man. We’re gonna take a knee," the coach said. "Now, I wanna pray for Jack and let’s keep him in our thoughts and prayers, man."

item.title: ChatGPT now lets you lock private chats with a PIN
item.description: OpenAI's new locked chats feature lets you protect ChatGPT conversations with a PIN, Face ID or Touch ID, but there are key privacy limitations.
item.content:encoded:
Ever handed someone your phone or let them use your computer to show them something, then suddenly worried about what else they might see? Maybe you've been using ChatGPT to work through a personal issue or plan a surprise for someone. Your conversation history can reveal quite a bit.

Now, OpenAI is giving you a way to keep certain conversations out of sight. The company just introduced Locked Chats, a new feature that lets you protect individual ChatGPT conversations with a four-digit PIN. On supported devices, you can also use Face ID, Touch ID or your phone's unlock method.

That sounds reassuring, especially as more people turn to artificial intelligence for personal advice. However, there are a few privacy limitations worth understanding before you start locking everything down. Here's how the feature works and how to set it up.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay and downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FAKE CHATGPT BILLING EMAILS CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN

OpenAI's new Locked Chats feature allows you to protect selected conversations without deleting them. Once you lock a chat, it moves into a separate area under Projects > Locked chats. The conversation disappears from your regular chat history, pinned chats and standard search results. Its title and contents stay behind your PIN until you choose to open them. You can even continue the conversation later without moving it back into your regular history.

Think about how useful that could be if you share a computer with your spouse or occasionally let someone use your phone. Perhaps you're researching an anniversary surprise and don't want the details popping up in your sidebar. Now, you have a way to keep that conversation separate.

There's one important detail if you already use ChatGPT Projects. Locking a conversation removes it from its original project. As a result, the conversation loses access to that project's instructions, files and memory. Even if you unlock it later, the conversation returns to your regular history rather than its previous project.

The feature is rolling out gradually to ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu users. It works on the web, in the iPhone and Android apps and in the new ChatGPT desktop apps for Mac and Windows. OpenAI says ChatGPT for Healthcare does not support Locked Chats.

You can lock an existing conversation in a few steps. The process is similar whether you're using ChatGPT on your computer, iPhone, Samsung Galaxy or Google Pixel.

Note: If you don't see Lock chat, the feature may not have reached your account yet. OpenAI is releasing it gradually. Some conversation types also cannot be locked.

Your conversation will move into Locked chats. The PIN belongs to your OpenAI account, so you can use the same PIN across supported devices where you're signed in.

Note: If you don't see Lock chat, the feature may not have reached your account yet. OpenAI is releasing it gradually. Some conversation types also cannot be locked.

META AI LAUNCHES PRIVATE INCOGNITO CHAT

Typing a PIN every time you want to open a personal conversation can get tiresome. Fortunately, OpenAI supports biometric authentication on compatible iPhones and device authentication on supported Android phones.

You can now use supported biometric authentication to access locked conversations on that iPhone. Your four-digit account PIN remains available as a backup.

Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel users follow the same steps inside the ChatGPT app. The available authentication method depends on your phone and its settings.

Once enabled, you can use your supported device unlock method to access protected conversations. Depending on your phone, that may include fingerprint recognition or another available authentication method.

This setting applies only to the device where you enable it. Turning on device authentication on your Galaxy or Pixel does not automatically enable it on another phone.

Once you've protected a chat, you'll probably want to return to it. Fortunately, OpenAI keeps your locked conversations in one dedicated location.

You can continue chatting as you normally would. Opening the conversation temporarily gives you access without permanently removing its protection. You can also start a brand-new conversation directly inside Locked chats. After opening that area with your PIN, simply enter a new message. It will remain in the protected section. However, there's a limitation worth knowing. OpenAI doesn't allow you to archive, pin, move or share a conversation while it's locked. You'll need to permanently unlock it before using those options. Anyone who can open a locked conversation can also copy its contents.

Yes, although the timing depends on your device. On iPhone, Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel, OpenAI says access ends automatically after you've been away from a locked chat or the Locked chats area for one minute. The same one-minute rule applies when the app runs in the background.

On the web, refreshing the page or closing the tab ends access. The desktop and web versions also relock after you've been away from the authorized window. If you want to secure everything immediately, select Lock now.

There's another detail worth knowing. A conversation may remain visible in the browser tab immediately after you lock it. Similarly, another device that's already running ChatGPT might temporarily display an older conversation title until it refreshes. So, check your screen before handing over your device.

You may eventually decide that a conversation no longer needs extra protection. You can return it to your normal history without deleting its contents.

The conversation returns to your regular history and can eventually appear in ordinary search results again.

Here's where I want you to pay close attention. Locking a conversation can stop someone casually browsing your chat history. However, OpenAI makes clear that Locked Chats do not provide end-to-end encryption or create a separate encrypted vault. The company also says locking a chat does not change how long it retains your information. Your existing Improve the model for everyone setting remains unchanged, too.

Memory introduces another consideration. If ChatGPT remembered something before you locked a conversation, that information can still exist in regular Memory. Once the chat is locked, new information remembered from subsequent messages stays within the Locked Chats memory area. Other locked conversations can use that information, but regular chats do not receive those new memories automatically. Locked chats can also draw on existing regular Memory when it's enabled.

There's also a potential surprise involving shared links. If you previously shared a conversation through a link, locking it does not revoke that link. Anyone with the existing link may still access the content that was previously shared. You must delete the shared link separately to stop that access.

Files come with their own limitations. Documents and other files uploaded or created inside a locked conversation receive the same protection as the chat itself. However, files already stored elsewhere in ChatGPT's Space or brought in from connected services keep their existing access permissions. Locking a conversation won't automatically protect those separate files.

For workplace accounts, existing organizational retention and compliance policies still apply. OpenAI says Enterprise and Edu conversation logs can include locked chats through its compliance tools. Workspace administrators cannot unlock your chats or reset your PIN, but authorized compliance systems may still access applicable conversation data.

These are important limitations if you're discussing financial information or other highly personal subjects. I would still avoid uploading passwords, Social Security numbers or complete banking credentials to a general ChatGPT conversation.

If you're concerned about how OpenAI handles your conversations, there's another privacy setting you should review. Turning off Improve the model for everyone prevents your new conversations from being used to train OpenAI's models. These instructions apply to personal ChatGPT accounts. OpenAI says content from ChatGPT Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces is not used to train its models by default.

Here's how to do it.

On the ChatGPT website

On iPhone, Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel

Your new conversations will no longer be used for model training after you turn off this setting. They can still remain in your chat history, so you'll need Locked Chats or another option to keep them out of view. For additional privacy controls across other AI services, see my guide on how to opt out of AI data collection in popular apps.

OpenAI already offers a feature called Temporary Chat, which serves a different purpose. Temporary Chats don't appear in your regular history or create new memories. OpenAI also excludes them from model training while they remain temporary. However, the company may retain temporary conversations for up to 30 days for safety purposes. Depending on your settings, a Temporary Chat can also use existing personalization information.

Locked Chats make more sense when you want to save a conversation and return to it later without leaving it exposed in your normal history. You can keep adding messages, and the conversation stays behind your PIN.

So, if you're having a one-time discussion you don't need to save, Temporary Chat may be the better choice. If you're working through something personal over several days, Locked Chats gives you a way to maintain that conversation with additional access protection.

This is one detail I really don't want you to overlook. Resetting a forgotten PIN permanently deletes all your locked chats, along with memories stored only within those chats and files or other content protected only by the previous PIN. OpenAI says the deletion cannot be undone. Even its support team cannot recover that protected content. If you remember your current PIN and simply want to change it, you can do so without losing your conversations.

If you've forgotten your PIN, you can also reset it from Settings > Security and login > Account PIN. However, you'll need to verify your identity and confirm the permanent deletion of your protected chats and associated content before creating a replacement PIN.

One more thing: OpenAI doesn't allow every conversation to be locked. The exclusions include Temporary Chats, archived chats, group chats and conversations created from shared links. Chats involving scheduled tasks, meeting recordings or background tasks are also excluded. The same applies to conversations with responses saved as project sources. Some Health, Codex and Work conversations have additional restrictions. If the Lock chat option doesn't appear, your conversation may not qualify.

I like that OpenAI is finally giving people more control over which conversations appear when someone opens ChatGPT. As AI becomes a place where people work through personal decisions, there's a real need for some discretion. Being able to hand someone your phone without exposing an entire conversation history is a useful improvement. Still, I would treat Locked Chats as a convenience and access-control feature rather than a guarantee of confidentiality. The four-digit PIN helps keep curious eyes away, but your broader privacy depends on the information you share and the settings you've chosen. And that leaves me wondering whether OpenAI should eventually offer something stronger for conversations people consider deeply private.

Would you trust ChatGPT with your most personal conversations if they were protected by a PIN, or should OpenAI offer stronger privacy protections before you feel comfortable sharing? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Christian McCaffrey gives one 49ers quality that separates team from pack amid Super Bowl hopes
item.description: Christian McCaffrey reveals why the San Francisco 49ers' veteran maturity gives them a massive advantage in their Super Bowl pursuit this season.
item.content:encoded:
There might be something a little bit different about this San Francisco 49ers team than in years past.

In this decade alone, the Niners have already played in two Super Bowls, and with their 6-1 record, they are in the conversation to be in yet another one.

Christian McCaffrey does not like "comparing teams," but the organization has had a similar nucleus in the front office, on the sidelines, and on the field.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I love the maturity of this team. Everyone talks about our age and how we’re old, but I think that’s such a massive advantage," McCaffrey told OutKick in a recent interview. "You’ve had guys who have been at the top of the top in this league and experienced the hardships, so you’ve seen everything. Emotionally, you’re not too amped when you win a game, and you’re not too down when something bad happens. There’s a level of professionalism in the locker room where we all know what we have to do."

Of course, that maturity helps in dealing with pressure and negativity as well.

"We just don’t care what people say. We’re here to win no matter what the situation is. From a noise perspective, we just don’t listen to it," he added. "This offseason, we were old and decrepit, and nobody thought we could win. Now, everybody’s crowning us. If you buy stock in listening to the media, you have to ride the highs and lows with them. We choose not to invest and just keep focusing on playing good football."

McCaffrey is still at the top of his game at age 30 and in his 10th NFL season, and it would not be possible without a health and wellness routine. But for the most part, he keeps it simple.

"Less is more. Getting outside, moving and having a healthy lifestyle. There’s not a one-trick-pony hack. There is no hack. There’s not a specific thing that’s going to get you to where you want to be. It’s consistency over time. That’s with training, recovery, nutrition, sleep, your environment, the people you’re around and how many stressors you allow in your life," McCaffrey said.

But of course, there’s always some additional help behind the scenes, and that’s where Dymatize Nutrition, of which McCaffrey is a brand partner, and its ISO100 protein come in.

"Nutrition plays such a key role in your recovery, how you feel and your training. Everything I put in my body, I’m conscious of. I want to put stuff in my body that’s going to help me recover better, not get as sore and allow me to have better days after hard workouts," McCaffrey said.

"I tested the product and absolutely loved it. Getting on a routine with the ISO100 and the different protein options they have has helped me in my training, recover quicker and continue to make strides even later in my career."

In order to bring back a long-awaited Lombardi Trophy back to the Bay Area, though, McCaffrey wants to "keep the main thing the main thing." And as cliché as it is, it truly is simply staying in routine day by day.

"Everybody wants to win the Super Bowl, but you don’t stay focused by sitting around thinking about winning the Super Bowl," he said. "You do that by waking up every day, having structure, having a routine and getting whatever needs to be done. If you have a collection of guys who do that, chances are you’re going to give yourself a chance."
